subject: ArrTags task 15.1 - Bounded log-subject policy and helper (ADR-026 clauses 1-2)

findings.description: ADR-026 clause 1 requires that a directory, drive, share, parent, or full path is never emitted, but every path test is POSIX-only. On the pinned Linux host Path.GetFileName does not treat a backslash as a separator, so a Windows-style string such as "C:\\dir\\share\\file.mkv" is returned and emitted verbatim (drive, share, and directories included). The worker records this as an interpretation/known limitation, but no test pins the platform semantics, so the clause-1 exclusion is verified only for host-native POSIX paths. The risk is documentation overclaim, not a reachable production leak: Jellyfin on the pinned Linux host reports POSIX paths.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs lines 21-47 use only POSIX absolute/relative paths
scratch probe against the built ArrTags.dll: LogSubject.Create(ItemId, "C:\\dir\\share\\file.mkv") -> "C:\\dir\\share\\file.mkv" (len 21); Path.GetFileName of the same -> the whole string
docs/implementation/15.1/reviewer-report.json finding 15.1-F1 reaches the same observation as INFORMATIONAL
findings.recommended_action: At 15.4, scope the documented clause-1 claim to host-native paths (state the POSIX/Linux verification explicitly), and add one assertion pinning the Linux backslash-is-literal behavior so the platform interpretation is recorded rather than incidental.

findings.description: Control-character removal is implemented with Rune.IsControl (Unicode Cc). Unicode Cf format characters such as U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE and U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE are emitted verbatim and are not covered by any test. ADR-026 clause 2 says 'control characters removed' without defining the category, so whether Cf should also be stripped is a 15.4 security-review decision and not a documented 15.1 requirement.
evidence: scratch probe: Create(ItemId, "/media/a\u202Eb.mkv") -> "a\u202Eb.mkv"; Create(ItemId, "/media/a\u200Bb.mkv") -> "a\u200Bb.mkv"; Rune.IsControl(U+202E)=False and Rune.IsControl(U+200B)=False
tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs ControlScalarsAreRemoved / EmittedSubjectContainsNoControlScalars cover C0/C1 (U+0000, U+0001, CR, LF, tab, U+0085, U+007F, U+009F) only
findings.recommended_action: The 15.4 logging security review should explicitly decide Cf handling; if Cc-only is intended, record that. No test change is required by ADR-026 as written.

findings.description: The fallback cases compare against ItemId.ToString("D", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture), mirroring the implementation, and the whole suite runs under DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT=1, so the tests cannot observe a regression from invariant to current culture. Guid 'D' formatting is inherently culture-independent, so there is no practical false-confidence risk. No flakiness source was found.
evidence: FallbackIsTheItemIdentifierInDFormat independently pins a 36-character value and Guid.TryParseExact(subject, "D", out parsed)

findings.description: A path containing a lone (unpaired) UTF-16 surrogate is not tested. EnumerateRunes silently substitutes U+FFFD, so the helper emits the replacement character rather than throwing; the result is deterministic and no host-native filesystem path can produce a lone surrogate, so this is an unreachable-input/documentation point rather than a behavior gap.
evidence: scratch probe: Create(ItemId, "/media/\uD83C.mkv") -> "\uFFFD.mkv" (len 5); a lone low surrogate behaves the same
findings.recommended_action: None required; optionally note in the 15.4 documentation that invalid UTF-16 input is replaced, not echoed.

findings.description: DocumentedMaximumIsTheAdrBound restates the literal 128 and is the only test that pins the literal ADR value; the at-bound, over-bound, and surrogate tests key off LogSubject.MaximumScalarValues and would not catch a changed constant on their own. This is an acceptable contract pin rather than a tautology, because the two styles together both pin the documented 128 and exercise its enforcement.
evidence: worker sensitivity probe 2: removing the bound break fails exactly NameBeyondTheBoundIsTruncatedToTheScalarBound, BoundNeverSplitsASurrogatePair, and BoundIsAppliedAfterControlRemoval, while NameAtTheBoundIsEmittedUnchanged still passes

summary: Independent audit of task 15.1. The helper is exercised on the real production path (direct LogSubject.Create calls, no doubles or mocks), and the assertions are exact-value and behavior-oriented. ADR-026 clauses 1-2 coverage is genuinely established: file-name-only extraction (5 POSIX cases plus a directory-segment fact, including the trailing-separator and separator-only fallbacks), the 128-Unicode-scalar bound (at-bound, over-bound, and a 200-astral-emoji case proving no surrogate split), Cc control removal (NUL/SOH, CR/LF, tab, U+0085 NEL, U+007F DEL, U+009F), otherwise-verbatim whitespace, fall-back on empty/whitespace/control-only/control-reduced-to-whitespace names, non-ASCII/combining/astral verbatim emission, and the Guid 'D' fallback independently pinned by length and Guid.TryParseExact. I reproduced the focused run (23/23, 0 skipped) and the full default suite (0 failed / 1517 passed / 63 skipped / 1580 total, matching the worker exactly; build 0 warnings / 0 errors). I recomputed each of the worker's five test-sensitivity probes against the test bodies: the expected failure sets are exactly 20/3, 3/20, 6/17, 3/20, and 5/18, matching the worker's counts, and I confirmed the affected edge behaviors empirically against the built assembly (including the single passing 'single.mkv' path case that makes probe 1 fail 20 rather than 21). No BLOCKER or HIGH finding: the shipped helper behavior is exercised and no test passes for the wrong reason. The open LOW finding is that the clause-1 drive/share/parent exclusion is verified only on POSIX paths (unreachable on the pinned Linux host but broader than any test); the remaining findings are INFORMATIONAL observations for the 15.4 security review (Cf format characters, culture, lone surrogates, the literal-constant pin). The documented build-and-release matrix still records the v1.1.0.0 baseline counts; the +23 cases are not reflected there, which is expected until the v1.2 release documentation task and is not a 15.1 defect. Verdict: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS.
